subject: Capacity onboarding timeline & minimum capacity guarantee for AtlasAI
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@atlasai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Capacity onboarding timeline & minimum capacity guarantee for AtlasAI

Jordan —

Thanks for the productive call earlier. As promised I'm sending three concrete reservation pathways so your engineering and procurement teams can evaluate tradeoffs (cost, time-to-scale, reliability). I've attached a one-page summary and the draft SOW. High level options:

- Option 1 — Small committed pool: 8x A100-80GB GPUs, minimum guarantee 4 GPUs. Fast onboarding (~2 weeks) and lowest upfront spend. Good for staging and early production with burst to hosted.
- Option 2 — Medium steady-state: 32x H100-80GB GPUs, minimum guarantee 8 GPUs. Better unit economics for 24/7 workloads, onboarding ~4 weeks with canary stages.
- Option 3 — Phased ramp to large cluster: start with 16x GPUs + dedicated burst, then ramp to 64x H100 over 8–12 weeks. Includes warm-up, KV cache seeding, and traffic-slicing policies.

A few operational notes:
- We recommend a 20% buffer pool above guaranteed min for prompt variance and prewarm.
- Autoscale policies: scale-from-min (guaranteed) up to committed max within 60s for queued requests; fallback routes to hosted variants if capacity exhausted.
- Recommended model variants: quantized medium-sized models for interactive endpoints and full-sized variants on background batch jobs.

Next steps: can you confirm which option you want to prioritize so we can lock pricing and draft the final SOW? Procurement contact copied here as discussed.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_capacity_options_v2.pdf, SOW-draft-AtlasAI.docx

From: Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@atlasai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-03T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity onboarding timeline & minimum capacity guarantee for AtlasAI

Hannah —

Thanks, this is helpful. Two questions from my engineering lead: 1) what do you mean by a 20% buffer pool in practice (is it reserved, billed, or pooled across teams?), and 2) can you share the expected latency SLOs for Option 2 at p95 under steady traffic (we have a 150ms soft target for chat inference).

Also procurement wants high-level payment terms (monthly/annual) and whether there are commit discounts if we sign for 12 months.

—Jordan
Jordan Meyers
Head of Infrastructure, AtlasAI
jordan.meyers@atlasai.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@atlasai.com>, Procurement <procure@atlasai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-04T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity onboarding timeline & minimum capacity guarantee for AtlasAI

Jordan — quick answers below, summary and attachments attached.

Buffer pool: reserved capacity (billed as part of the committed cluster) set aside as a soft buffer to handle burst and cache pre-warm. Practically: if you commit 32 GPUs and set min=8, we recommend setting buffer=6 (20% of 32) so the scheduling engine prefers keeping that capacity available for transient spikes and warm-KV seeding. Buffer is configurable; you only pay for the committed cluster size, not additionally for temporary hosted bursts.

Latency SLOs (Option 2 - 32x H100):
- Typical p50: 18–32 ms for single-turn short chat requests (<=256 tokens)
- p95: ~110–160 ms depending on model and sequence length; for your target 150ms p95 we recommend using the LlamaX-medium quantized variant for interactive routes.

Commit terms / discounts:
- Monthly: standard rate (no minimum term) — higher per-unit cost.
- 12-month: 12% discount on committed capacity over listed per-GPU rates.
- 24-month: 18% discount + extended SLA credits.

I've attached the GPU cost breakdown workbook that maps the different cluster configs to expected monthly token throughput and unit cost. If you're comfortable, we can pencil in Option 2 with min=8 and buffer=6 and circulate an SOW for signature.

Hannah

Attachments: gpu-cost-breakdown.xlsx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@atlasai.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-05T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity onboarding timeline & minimum capacity guarantee for AtlasAI

Jordan — quick tech note from the infra side to make the ramp predictable. I’ve sketched an operational onboarding plan below (we can drop into the SOW):

- Week 0–1: Provision 32 H100s in your dedicated tenant, baseline network VPC peering and KMS integration. Smoke tests.
- Week 2: Deploy canary traffic slices (10% production) to verify latency and warm KV cache seeding. Collect perf telemetry to tune kernel selection.
- Week 3–4: Move to 50% traffic, enable autoscale thresholds and prewarm top-100 prompt keys.
- Week 5–8: Full cutover to committed cluster. Continue QoS tuning; enable fallback routes to hosted for non-critical paths.

Minimums and autoscale details:
- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 8 (will be billed as minimum even if idle).
- Burst strategy: allow burst to committed max (32) for queued requests with fair-share shaping and token-based throttles.
- Warm-up: we seed KV cache in the first two weeks for the top traffic patterns to reduce p95 variance.

Operational actions we need from AtlasAI:
- Provide 1–2 sample prompt sets and expected 95th percentile lengths.
- Create a procurement contact for contract circulation.

If you're aligned we can convert this timeline into the SOW milestones and start procurement.

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

From: Procurement <procure@atlasai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-06T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Capacity onboarding timeline & minimum capacity guarantee for AtlasAI

Hannah / Vivek —

Thanks for the clear options. We discussed internally and want to proceed with Option 2 (32x H100), min guarantee 8 GPUs, buffer set to 6. Procurement prefers annual billing with the 12% commit discount; please send a formal SOW and the contract redline template. Also confirm lead times (we're targeting Go-Live by end of March).

Jordan (cc'd) will share sample prompt sets by EOD Monday. Once we have the SOW we can start our internal approval flow.
